the_report_pass_landed_before_the_number: Same ordering discipline daedalus/mixture_opt.py was written under, and for the same reason: the candidate arms are not trained yet, so nothing in `report` can have been fitted to their results. It recomputes each arm's aggregate under evaluation_weights rather than reading metrics.bpb off the card, which makes 'one weighting for every arm' true by construction; the card's own figure then becomes a free consistency check, and an equal-weighted card is visibly inconsistent rather than quietly rankable against the others.
four_refusals_in_report: (1) a card that scored only part of the corpus -- the aggregate is an average over the corpus and the per-source regression check compares source by source, and neither is defined on a subset; (2) a card whose details.train_weights differ from the arm now bearing its name, which is reachable because `derive` is legitimately re-runnable and a re-derivation renormalizes EVERY share, while the run directory, scorecard name and tag all still match; (3) a card whose recorded aggregate disagrees with the recomputed one beyond 1e-9; (4) a report built with derived=None, which candidate_arms would render as a two-arm comparison describing itself as the comparison of three.

The revision the corpus actually builds stack-edu-python from -- codeparrot/github-code at refs/convert/parquet, sha b88aff789d4fe05af7cd4faa78cdfe855930e40c -- carries NO license on its card, while the dataset's default revision reports ['other']. what_the_drops_block_fixes: Of n_seen documents, why did n_seen - n_kept not make it? Previously unanswerable.
